briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax-Relief Politics Heat Up in Lansing as Psychedelics Hit the FDA's Main Stage
briefs.top: Michigan operators just got real political cover: GOP governor nominee John James is staking his campaign on killing the 24% wholesale tax, and a bipartisan repeal bill is already sitting in the Legislature. Nationally, psychedelics take center stage this week as the FDA holds its first-ever public hearing on therapeutic use while Compass Pathways edges toward what could be the first approved psilocybin medicine.

local.text: GOP governor nominee John James is courting Michigan cannabis donors with a pledge to repeal or sharply reduce the state's 24% wholesale tax — a signal operators finally have a serious ally in Lansing's biggest race, with a JARS Cannabis-hosted fundraiser alone netting his campaign nearly $90,000.

A Republican state rep has introduced HB 6224 to repeal the tax outright, and lawmakers from both parties are now backing repeal proposals, arguing the levy has generated less revenue than promised while piling pressure on licensed operators.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is pushing the retail format forward, targeting a fall opening for a dispensary paired with a full-service restaurant — a hospitality-first buildout that goes further than most Michigan stores have dared.

JARS Cannabis notched a regulatory win in Madison Heights, getting a Flock license-plate camera removed near one of its stores — a small but real sign operators can push back on surveillance overreach.

Higher Love closed five of its nine Upper Peninsula stores under the weight of the wholesale tax, but crosstown operator Rize is proving there's a playbook: negotiating cost-sharing arrangements with suppliers to split the tax burden and keep growing.

national.text: The FDA holds its first-ever public hearing tomorrow, Sept. 14, on the potential future therapeutic use of psychedelic drugs — part of the Trump administration's push under Executive Order 14401 to accelerate research and review of psilocybin, MDMA and LSD therapies.

Rescheduling just got sturdier: a legal challenge to the April order moving medical marijuana to Schedule III was rebuffed this week, with the D.C. Circuit leaving the reclassification order in effect on Sept. 9.

Compass Pathways' synthetic psilocybin COMP360 was awarded the FDA's Commissioner's National Priority Voucher and a granted rolling NDA review for treatment-resistant depression, teeing up a possible first-ever approved psychedelic medicine.

Cross-border consolidation is now live: Curaleaf's bid for Canada's Aurora Cannabis signals a U.S. MSO chasing a Canadian target with a realistic path to closing, powered by the improving capital backdrop since partial federal rescheduling.

The DEA's full Schedule I-to-III rescheduling hearing wrapped its formal proceedings over the summer, and though no final decision has landed yet, the process keeps grinding toward a ruling that would reshape banking, taxes and interstate commerce for the whole industry.
